title: bot.ability.reasoning.recalled
description: Private completion: memory recall finished; ready to dispatch the processor.

turn.description: The body's processing turn this event belongs to, counted from 1 [floppy field].

host_input.description: Processing input: stimulus payload plus HSM event schemas available for selection. Processor output is always an array of selected events.

instructions.description: Optional system policy stamped by Processing for model-facing processors. Not part of the stimulus; providers use this as the system prompt when present.
examples: Return an immediate typed result only when the input is already unambiguous.
instructions.title: Instructions

host_input.title: InputData

items.description: Recallable cognition episode (JSON in memory, query_tags=cognitive_episode). Used when reflection chooses bot.behavior.create / change / break.

heard.description: The words the turn's stimulus carried, in the order it carried them, each once: the content of each message of a text type in it, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes in all, cut at a whole word; empty when it carried none [floppy field].
heard.title: Heard

images.description: The images the turn's stimulus carried, in the order it carried them, each once, at most 8: each its reference and media type, as the stimulus carried it (decision D252); left out when it carried none [floppy field].

image.description: Reference (a URI reference) to the image; floppy passes media by reference, never as bytes [floppy field].
image.title: Image

media_type.description: The image's media type, such as image/png, or null when the stimulus gave none.
media_type.title: Media Type

images.title: Images

outcome.description: How a failed or cancelled turn ended (decision D139); a completed turn's episode has none [floppy field].
outcome.title: Outcome

failure.description: Why a failed turn failed; null for a cancelled one (decision D139) [floppy field].
failure.title: Failure

output.description: Typed cognitive output from that prior turn.

items.description: One selected modeled HSM event. Processing dispatches it to the resolved target fire-and-forget; hosts do not re-apply OutputData. Put selection rationale on reason here — not on the event payload.

examples.reason: Attention should move to that device for this turn.

anyOf.description: Stable reference used by a cognition host to resolve a target or modeled event.

target.description: Stable reference for the host-local receiver of the modeled event. Hosts may omit this when the event resolves relative to focus or a single actor.
target.title: Target

event.description: Canonical modeled HSM event name selected by cognition.
event.title: Event

data.description: Optional typed domain payload for the selected event. Model and learned-behavior JSON projections omit raw media. Do not put selection rationale here — use reason on this envelope.
data.title: Data

reason.description: Optional reason this event was selected.
examples: Attention should move to that device for this turn.
reason.title: Reason

items.title: EventData

output.title: Output

anyOf.description: Create a new executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the create write step must author full Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API and the observed pattern — not by copying canned examples. The source's lifetime decides how it runs: a turn behavior (default) answers one matching turn; a persistent routine (lifetime = "persistent") keeps running on hsm.every / hsm.at schedules across turns and restarts, for recurring or time-based needs or when the user asked for something recurring.

examples.description: Say hello when a knock sound arrives.
examples.name: GreetOnKnock
examples.reason: Same knock→greeting pattern across recent episodes.

examples.description: Persistent routine: brief the user at 08:00 on weekdays.
examples.name: MorningBriefing
examples.reason: The user asked to hear a briefing every weekday morning.

name.description: Stable PascalCase behavior / HSM model name to install.
name.title: Name

triggers.description: External environment event names that may propose this behavior to fast intuition. Installed on the inventory instance alongside the Starlark program's own triggers.
triggers.title: Triggers

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the behavior does, shown in inventory and reflection. The install keeps the caller-supplied description when present.
examples: Say hello when a knock sound arrives.
description.title: Description

reason.description: Why this behavior is being installed now: the observed pattern across recent episodes that justifies it. Recorded for reflection, never dispatched.
examples: Same knock→greeting pattern across recent episodes.
reason.title: Reason

source.description: Starlark HSM behavior source authored for this install. Required on the create write step. Must declare input_event, output_event, and behavior = hsm.define(Name, ...) (or behavior_program(...)) with string-named callbacks. Invent names, schemas, guards, and effects from the observed pattern using the Starlark behavior API. A persistent routine also sets lifetime = "persistent" and schedules transitions with hsm.every / hsm.at. Select intent may omit this field.
source.title: Source

anyOf.title: CreateData

anyOf.description: Change an existing executable behavior. Select may omit source (intent only); the change write step must author full revised Starlark HSM source from the behavior Starlark API, the existing behavior, and the observed pattern. Changing a persistent routine (for example its schedule) restarts it with the revised source; the lifetime global may also turn a behavior into a routine or back.

name.description: Stable name of the behavior to revise.
name.title: Name

triggers.description: Replacement external event names that may propose this behavior to fast intuition. Installed on the inventory instance alongside the revised Starlark program.
triggers.title: Triggers

description.description: Revised human-readable summary of what the behavior does, shown in inventory and reflection. The install keeps the caller-supplied description when present.
examples: Say hello when a knock sound arrives, after clearing focus.
description.title: Description

reason.description: Why this behavior is being revised now: the observed gap or regression the revision fixes. Recorded for reflection, never dispatched.
reason.title: Reason

source.description: Revised Starlark HSM behavior source. Required on the change write step. Must remain a valid executable behavior declaration whose model name matches this behavior name. Author revisions from the Starlark behavior API and existing_behavior.source — do not paste unrelated canned source. Keep lifetime = "persistent" and its hsm.every / hsm.at schedules for a routine.
source.title: Source

anyOf.title: ChangeData

anyOf.description: Break a behavior that no longer improves (or harms) robot behavior. Sets inventory status=BROKEN so Autonomy will not run it and a persistent routine stops; the row remains for a later bot.behavior.change repair. Optional reason becomes status_reason.

examples.name: GreetOnKnock
examples.reason: Greeted while the bot was already mid-conversation.

name.description: Stable name of the behavior to set status=BROKEN.
name.title: Name

reason.description: Why this behavior is being retired: the observed harm or staleness. Becomes the inventory status_reason so a later change can repair it.
examples: Greeted while the bot was already mid-conversation.
reason.title: Reason

anyOf.title: BreakData

behavior.description: Behavior create/change/break payload recorded with this episode, if any.
behavior.title: Behavior

items.title: CognitiveEpisode

items.description: Recallable standing directive (JSON in memory, query_tags=standing_directive). What the bot was told; it stays recalled until it is removed from memory.

examples.text: Call Bob when you get a chance.

text.description: The instruction exactly as the bot was told it, in plain language.
examples: Call Bob when you get a chance.
text.title: Text

kind.description: Memory classification written on the directive row.
kind.title: MemoryClassificationKind

items.title: Directive

input.description: Live body input for this turn: the stimulus plus the abilities, named actors, and focus candidates the stage may select from. Built by the Cognition host from live body context.

focus.description: Instance name the bot is looking at, if any.
focus.title: Focus

focus_candidates.description: Instance names that may become focus for this turn (body attention policy).
focus_candidates.title: Focus Candidates

input.title: InputData
